record.paper_title: Constructive Field Theory and Applications: Perspectives and Open Problems
record.original_question: Construct the nontrivial renormalization-group fixed point for a solid-on-solid interface model with two competing exponentials, at least in the regime where the fixed point is close to a Gaussian one.

evidence.quote: An important open problem is to construct the non-trivial renormalization group fixed point for a solid-on-solid model of an interface with two competing exponentials. This should be doable at least in the regime where this fixed point is closed to a Gaussian one

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a solid-on-solid (SOS) model of a one-dimensional fluctuating interface above a wall, in which the height variable $\phi(x)$ (defined on a lattice or as a continuum field on $\mathbb{R}^d$) is governed by a Gaussian free-field action perturbed by two competing exponential potentials, with formal action
$$S[\phi] \;=\; \tfrac{1}{2}\int (\nabla\phi)^2\,dx \;+\; \int\!\bigl(g_1\,e^{\alpha_1 \phi(x)} + g_2\,e^{\alpha_2 \phi(x)}\bigr)\,dx,$$
where $\alpha_1,\alpha_2$ are real charges (with opposite signs, modeling attraction to and repulsion from the wall) and $g_1,g_2>0$ are coupling constants. Under a Wilsonian renormalization-group flow that integrates out short-distance modes of $\phi$, the couplings $(g_1,g_2)$ flow in a two-dimensional space.

Construct rigorously a non-trivial (nonzero) fixed point of this renormalization-group flow, at least in the perturbative regime where the fixed point lies arbitrarily close to the Gaussian (free-field) fixed point. That is, prove the existence of an analytic RG transformation acting on a suitable Banach space of effective potentials and exhibit a nontrivial fixed point of this transformation that bifurcates from the Gaussian fixed point as the relevant parameters cross their critical values, providing a mathematically rigorous description of the wetting/depinning critical point of the two-exponential SOS model.
artifact.category_tag: Constructive renormalization group / wetting fixed point
artifact.status_search_result: Functional/heuristic renormalization-group analyses of wetting transitions with competing potentials are well established in the physics literature (e.g., Lipowsky–Fisher), exhibiting nontrivial fixed points in suitable scaling regimes. However, no rigorous constructive-field-theory construction of the nontrivial RG fixed point for the two-competing-exponential SOS interface model near the Gaussian fixed point has been located; the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Scaling regimes and functional renormalization for wetting transitions
status_evidence.snippet: Functional RG acts as a nonlinear map in the space of interaction potentials V(l); in the SFL regime two nontrivial fixed-point potentials V*₀ and V*c are found describing the delocalized phase and the unbinding critical manifold.
status_evidence.claim: Heuristic functional RG analyses identify nontrivial wetting fixed points, but these are not rigorous constructions.

status_evidence.title: A Complete Renormalization Group Trajectory Between Two Fixed Points
status_evidence.snippet: Rigorous constructive RG trajectories between fixed points have been built in related models, illustrating the type of constructive result sought.
status_evidence.claim: Constructive RG fixed-point results exist for related models but not specifically for the two-exponential SOS wetting model.
